sentences.text: Housing Board (KHB) for formation of a residential layout.
The preliminary notification was issued - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:37299 AND 1 OTHER in the year 2011, the final notification was issued on 24.06.2013 and the award has been passed on 02.09.2015.
Thereafter, possession has been taken and 16(2) notification has been issued on 30.12.2020.

2. The petitioners have challenged the same on the ground that the award has not been passed within two years and the scheme has hence lapsed and the acquisition proceedings is liable to be set aside.
It is also urged that the possession has not been taken and the petitioners are still in possession of the property.
On the said ground, it is prayed that the acquisition proceedings should be set aside.

3. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-KHB submits that though the proceedings were initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the proceedings have concluded after coming into effect of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the Act').

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted that the compensation is - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:37299 AND 1 OTHER being awarded to the land losers as per the new enactment.

It is further submitted that, as contemplated under Section 25 of the new Act, extension of time has been granted for passing of the award and within the said stipulated date of extension, the award has been passed and the amount has been deposited before the Reference Court.
It is also submitted that there is a dispute as to ownership of the land and the ownership of the petitioners are disputed.
It is also submitted that possession has been taken and a notification is also issued regarding the same, apart from the drawing up of mahazar.
The notification is dated 30.12.2020.
4. The petitioners are not in a position to contravene the aforementioned submission of the learned counsel for the respondent-KHB.

5. In the course of the arguments, the learned counsel for the respondent-KHB, upon instructions,
also submits that the respondent-KHB is agreeable to offer 50% of developed land to be formed taking into consideration the - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:37299 AND 1 OTHER area acquired from the petitioners (subject to they establishing their title) as compensation in lieu of monetary compensation if they so desired.
6. Further, it is noticed that there is a delay of six years in filing the writ petition since passing of the award.
The said delay is also not satisfactorily explained by the petitioners.

As preliminary Sri N Narayanappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173204395/
11 notification and final notification are issued in accordance with law, the award is passed within the extended period as contemplated under the Act, as the possession of the property has already been taken over as contemplated in law and the respondent-KHB is offering the land losers compensation under the new enactment Act, or if they desired 50% of the developed sites as per the policy of the State, I do not see any reason to interfere in the action of the respondents in acquiring the property.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Housing Board (KHB) for formation of a residential layout.
The preliminary notification was issued - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:37299 AND 1 OTHER in the year 2011, the final notification was issued on 24.06.2013 and the award has been passed on 02.09.2015.
Thereafter, possession has been taken and 16(2) notification has been issued on 30.12.2020.
2. The petitioners have challenged the same on the ground that the award has not been passed within two years and the scheme has hence lapsed and the acquisition proceedings is liable to be set aside.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
On the said ground, it is prayed that the acquisition proceedings should be set aside.
3. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-KHB submits that though the proceedings were initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the proceedings have concluded after coming into effect of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the Act').
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
6. Further, it is noticed that there is a delay of six years in filing the writ petition since passing of the award.
The said delay is also not satisfactorily explained by the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.decision:
As preliminary Sri N Narayanappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173204395/
11 notification and final notification are issued in accordance with law, the award is passed within the extended period as contemplated under the Act, as the possession of the property has already been taken over as contemplated in law and the respondent-KHB is offering the land losers compensation under the new enactment Act, or if they desired 50% of the developed sites as per the policy of the State, I do not see any reason to interfere in the action of the respondents in acquiring the property.
7. For the aforementioned reasons, the Writ Petitions subject to the observations made herein above are hereby dismissed.
. All pending I.A.'s does not survive for consideration.
Hence, all pending I.A.'s are hereby dismissed.
